units.title: How Language Models Work
units.outcome: Explain how training changes a model and how that model generates an answer.
units.activity: Trace one answer through tokenisation and generation, then propose changes for new Sunday hours, brief answers and live catalogue availability. Explain where information goes, whether parameters change, required materials and a test. Add one material needed to investigate original training.
units.criteria: Explain the generation loop and fixed weights during ordinary inference. Distinguish request context, retrieval, training and tool execution; connect each intervention to necessary materials and an appropriate test. Explain a researcher’s additional need.
outcomes: Explain how training changes a model and how that model generates an answer.

units.title: What ‘Open’ Means
units.outcome: Distinguish a model release from a hosted application or model service.
units.activity: Assess Cedar and Rowan against the library’s adaptation and sharing requirements. Recommend a deployment route, cite the supplied terms, identify an unresolved practical question and a revision condition.
units.criteria: Trace who operates the model; cite permissions and restrictions; distinguish absent from uninspected information; explain practical fit and a feasible next check.
outcomes: Distinguish a model release from a hosted application or model service.
Assess release materials and terms, including open weights and open-source AI.
Recommend a release and deployment route for a purpose, with unresolved checks.
